questions.q: Ethyl butanoate is treated with sodium metal in absolute ethanol, followed by aqueous work-up. The products are:
questions.explain: Bouveault–Blanc reduction turns the acyl carbon into CH₂OH and releases the alkoxy part as its alcohol. The β-keto ester is the Claisen condensation product, which needs sodium ethoxide (a base), not sodium metal.

questions.q: How many sodium atoms are consumed, in the ideal equation, to reduce one molecule of an ester RCOOR′ to RCH₂OH and R′OH?
questions.explain: Taking the ester carbon to CH₂OH needs four electrons, one from each Na: RCOOR′ + 4Na + 2C₂H₅OH → RCH₂ONa + R′ONa + 2C₂H₅ONa. In practice excess Na is used because some is lost as H₂.

questions.q: An ester is treated with sodium in an aprotic solvent with no alcohol present. The product is:
questions.explain: Without a proton donor the radical-anion intermediates couple instead of being reduced, giving the acyloin condensation. Ethanol as proton source is what makes it a reduction.

questions.q: Ethyl oleate (which has one C=C in its chain) is reduced with Na and absolute ethanol. Which statement about the product is correct?
options: The C=C is reduced and the ester survives
Both the C=C and the ester are reduced, giving octadecan-1-ol
The ester is reduced to oleyl alcohol and the C=C survives
The product is oleic acid, because Na/EtOH only hydrolyses esters
questions.explain: In Bouveault and Blanc's original 1903 example, ethyl oleate gave oleyl alcohol with the chain C=C intact; isolated C=C bonds are not reduced by Na/EtOH (nor by LiAlH₄).
